title: DOM elements in a Qt Widgets window
blurb: A Qt Widgets app paints with Qt's raster engine and copies the result to a 2D canvas. Real <input>, <select> and <textarea> elements are drawn into that canvas with drawElementImage() after each flush.
question: Qt Widgets windows are painted in software and copied to a 2D canvas with putImageData(). Can drawElementImage() after each copy put live DOM elements in such a window?
result: Yes. The page wraps putImageData() on Qt's canvas and draws the elements after it. In a 2D canvas the draw also sets the hit box, so no geometry call is needed.
